headline: Media sees revenue growth but cost cuts, gaming balances profit pressure with tech spend, publishing is mixed, education shows divergent trends.
summary: Disney and WBD posted revenue gains while tightening IT budgets and pursuing cost cuts. Bally's grew strongly in gaming, yet Caesars widened losses. Wolters Kluwer and Pearson invest in AI and digital platforms, while Scholastic missed revenue. In education, Pearson and NYU expand tech spend, but SLU cuts staff.

industries.summary: Disney posted 8% revenue growth and a 43% jump in operating income. WBD delivered modest earnings on flat revenue. Versant added streaming channels and kept guidance. Cost‑cutting dominates the agenda.

leaders.why: Revenue up 8% and operating income up 43%

laggards.why: Revenue growth slowed and margin low at 5.2%

themes.title: Cost‑cutting
themes.detail: Disney targets $3 bn savings by 2029; WBD plans $6 bn annual cuts post‑merger.

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney explores AI in parks; Versant expands FAST channels and streaming memberships.

themes.title: Digital rebuild
themes.detail: Versant added four FAST channels and launched a new streaming membership.

industries.it_note: IT budgets are being trimmed as companies pursue $3‑$6 bn cost‑saving programs, though some digital initiatives continue.

industries.summary: Caesars posted $2.94 bn revenue but a $123 m loss. Bally's revenue jumped 21.7% with strong interactive growth. Light & Wonder focuses on debt reduction, Brightstar rolls out new lottery tech.

leaders.why: Revenue up 21.7% YoY driven by interactive segments

laggards.why: Widened net loss despite revenue growth

themes.title: Digital revenue growth
themes.detail: Bally's sees 5%+ digital revenue lift; Brightstar unveiled next‑gen lottery solutions.

themes.title: Cost‑cutting pressure
themes.detail: Light & Wonder prioritises debt reduction; Caesars tightens IT spend.

themes.title: AI skepticism
themes.detail: Caesars’ CEO says AI won’t replace face‑to‑face meetings.

industries.it_note: Most operators are tightening IT spend while allocating funds to digital platform upgrades.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer expands with AI partnerships and an AgileMD acquisition. Scholastic missed revenue and widened losses. Pearson shows accelerated growth and AI‑driven product launches.

leaders.why: Accelerated revenue growth and AI‑powered learning platform

laggards.why: Revenue miss and operating loss expansion

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer partners with Viz.ai; Pearson rolls out AI English platform and testing AI personas.

themes.title: M&A activity
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer acquires AgileMD for up to $100 m.

themes.title: Revenue pressure
themes.detail: Scholastic reports a $216.8 m miss and a -3.9% YoY decline.

industries.it_note: Investments in AI and digital platforms are driving an expanding IT spend outlook.

industries.summary: Pearson and NYU receive sizable public AI and quantum funding and expand tech programs. SLU cuts custodial staff and outsources services. ACT shows mixed performance with no clear tech signal.

leaders.why: Strong revenue growth and AI‑driven product expansion

themes.title: AI & quantum funding
themes.detail: NYU awarded $29.2 m for a quantum fab and $30 m city investment.

themes.title: Outsourcing moves
themes.detail: SLU outsources custodial services after campus layoffs.

themes.title: Mixed performance metrics
themes.detail: ACT reports state‑by‑state score variations with no clear trend.

industries.it_note: While Pearson and NYU expand tech spend, SLU’s outsourcing signals a tightening of internal IT resources.
